analysis: Integration review of units 45-81. Units 45-78 are slices of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json: synthetic golden vectors (fixture-scope, date 2028-02-29, public filler text) with no secrets, keys or consumer data. The patch adds template_input.additional_context.enable_thinking=false and regenerates token counts, chain hashes and token IDs (803->767, 862->826, 765->767, 824->826) for the Qwen JSON-format cases. The trailing token change (198 -> 271, 248069, 271) matches the closed empty think block. The provider changes (units 79-80) are in MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine+Translation.swift and ChatTemplateControls+Decoding.swift. A new branch defaults enable_thinking=false for JSON response_format on the Qwen35 template family only when the caller gave no thinking control, effort or budget. reasoning.max_tokens is decoded with try? and kept only if a positive Int, so malformed values degrade to nil with no unbounded or injectable value. withPromptDate now copies self, which preserves raw evidence fields. Units 81 are tests only. No change touches TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011, App Attest or encryption paths, keys, billing, or cache storage. Indirect relevance is T-041: prompt-rendering changes alter chain hashes, but the cache scope is coordinator-authored from account, model build and prompt-contract ID, and callers cannot influence it. Doc diffs (test.md, inference.md) say the vectors are regenerated in darkbloom-platform and checked by scripts/verify-prompt-parity.sh. Unverified, outside the supplied evidence: that the platform prompt sidecar mirrors the Swift rule and the budget semantics, which affects cache-plan parity and availability rather than confidentiality. The prompt_contract_id is unchanged although rendering changed. This is plausibly intended, since the contract ID is rendering-independent, but I could not confirm it. Part of the integration replay was omitted (181 units), and the fixture patch excerpt is truncated. I found no concrete security regression.
